title: A passing npm run ci leaves no build a sibling can pin
foundBy: user report (host): "it doesn't seem possible anymore to have make repin do pin on local builds, which haven't been published to ghcr.io or npmjs.com or built in the Github CI builds"

evidence.verified: `npm run ci` at 4332859 ended `record-build: recorded ui 4332859 as a local build in ~/.local/share/cs-builds/codesweep-ai (npm @codesweep-ai/ui@0.3.1-dev.20260926051938.4332859)`. dashboards' tests/test_record_build.py passes all 15 of its tests against this same scripts/record-build.sh, byte for byte. GitHub CI's `ci` passed on 4332859.

resolution: A clean, passing `npm run ci` now records its commit in the owner's build store, `~/.local/share/cs-builds/<owner>/`. It keeps the Go module in the module proxy's layout, the npm packages where the project has them, and an entry naming the versions. A run over uncommitted changes records nothing, and says so.
details: `npm run ci` runs every gate CI runs, on this machine, and leaves nothing another project can pin. Pins move only to commits GitHub CI lists as built. So a change across several projects has to be pushed and built one project at a time before the next can pin it. A clean passing run could record its commit as a local build instead: the npm package it publishes, and an entry naming its versions. They would go in a store the sibling projects read. Go and npm builds of a clean commit are byte-identical to CI's. A pin on such a build is therefore the pin CI writes once that commit is pushed.
